videos.label: StatQuest with Josh Starmer — The Difference Between Technical and Biological Replicates
videos.assignment: Watch only 0:36–1:03, then 2:19–2:59 (1:07 total). Two short introductory examples distinguish repeated measurement of one sample from measurement across biological sources. Skip the opening, the accuracy/precision conflation, broad demographic analogies and the experiment-specific RNA-seq recommendation. Repetition can quantify measurement variability but does not by itself remove systematic bias. Translate the distinction to the question’s independent unit: repeated seeds/runs on one benchmark are not additional independent datasets or participants. Terminology and replication level depend on the study design; the biological example is an analogy, not a universal classification rule.
